sections.h2: Where in Roxboro do I take a deed to be filed?
sections.html:
Person County keeps its deed records at 21 Abbitt Street, Roxboro, NC 27573. The county directory gives (336) 597-1733 for calls, and the Tax Office you will also visit is on the same street at number 13.

The department describes its purpose as keeping safe the most important papers of the county and its residents. Its service list covers:

  • land record searches
  • birth, death and marriage records
  • marriage licenses and notary oaths
  • military discharges, cemetery records, grave removals, plats and genealogy files

Two of these touch a home sale: the search that shows who holds a parcel and what is filed against it, and the filing that carries title to the buyer. Call for counter hours and any electronic filing option before you go.

sections.h2: What authority stands behind the Person County deed office?
sections.html:
Voters choose the register of deeds every two years (G.S. 161-1). Staff accept conveyances, apply the fixed statewide fees, and collect the excise tax before filing (G.S. 161-10).

Clerks index what arrives in order of arrival, and that order settles priority fights. G.S. 47-18 makes a deed, or a lease longer than three years, ineffective against lien creditors and paying buyers until it is registered where the land lies.

Staff cannot draft your deed or rule on a dispute over ownership. A signed deed left in a drawer protects you from nothing, so ask your closing attorney to confirm the filing on the day the money moves.

sections.h2: What fees does a Person County filing incur?
sections.html:
The legislature fixed every figure below, so nothing changes at the Roxboro counter.

Statewide filing charges applied in Roxboro (G.S. 161-10)
FilingCharge
Deed or other general instrument, 15 pages$26.00
Page 16 onward, general instruments$4.00 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage, 35 pages$64.00
Release of a deed of trustNo fee
Map or plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 per page after
Document in nonstandard form$25.00 extra
Additional instrument within one document$10.00 each

Payment comes before filing. Clearing an old loan before listing saves a little, since its release carries no charge.

sections.h2: Who owes the excise stamp tax on a Roxboro deed?
sections.html:
The seller, as the party giving up title, pays it to the register before the deed is filed. G.S. 105-228.30 prints the rate as $1.00 on each $500.00 or fractional part of the consideration or value conveyed.

The county keeps half. The rest, less refunds and a handling allowance, goes to the state each month. When a tract lies in several counties, the one with the greatest value collects.

  • On an ordinary sale it comes out of the seller's proceeds, so list it on your net sheet.
  • It follows the price or value stated, so it follows your contract.
  • For a gift or a deed between relatives, ask the office how it handles little or no stated consideration.

Have your closing attorney give you the exact amount in writing before closing day.

sections.h2: What should I look for in Person County land records before listing?
sections.html:
Spend an hour in the index, or have an attorney do it, and look for anything that blocks a clean handoff. Typical finds are old loans never released, judgments, and options or contracts filed years ago.

  • The name on the last recorded deed should match every seller.
  • The legal description in your contract should match the one in that deed.
  • Each earlier deed of trust needs a recorded release.
  • The Tax Office can quote the balance so the tax lien clears at closing.

Seller-financed deals follow Chapter 47H, which has the seller record the contract, or a short memorandum, within five business days.

A missing release is usually fixed with a call to the old lender. An owner who died with no estate opened needs the clerk of court first. A cash buyer can move quickly, but the title must still be cleaned up before anyone can insure it.

sections.h2: How should I prepare a deed for filing?
sections.html:
Bring the original signed and notarized deed, the tax payment and the fee, and check the page count. Every added page costs four dollars, so confirm that each exhibit is needed.

Sequence matters at closing. The buyer's lender normally files its deed of trust right after the deed, and releases for your payoff loans should already be moving.

  • Check the notary block for a complete date and signature.
  • Add the parcel number to page one if your attorney does.
  • Keep a stamped copy showing the time of registration.

Ask the Person County office whether it takes electronic filing, and get its counter hours before you drive over.

faqs.a: 21 Abbitt Street, Roxboro, NC 27573. The county directory lists (336) 597-1733, and the office can give you counter hours.

faqs.q: What does a deed filing run?
faqs.a: The statute prices a deed at $26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page. See the table above for loans, plats and copies.

faqs.q: Who pays the stamp tax when a home sells?
faqs.a: The seller does, to the register, before filing. The statute's rate is $1.00 per $500.00 or part of the value.

faqs.q: Do I pay to record the release of my old mortgage?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists no charge for releases of deeds of trust or mortgages.

faqs.q: Why does the filing time matter?
faqs.a: Priority follows the time of registration, and an unfiled conveyance loses to lien creditors and paying buyers.
